findings: All17 bounded helper/compiled-template cases pass in Chromium153, Firefox155 and WebKit26.6. Firefox uses the selected scoped registry polyfill, not native scoped support.

Successful cases include canonical/order overlap, same-value reassertion, one complete transaction notification, invalid numeric rollback, explicit{}clear, expression removal/replacement ownership, disconnected root part writes, real Lit cache retention/restoration, actual helper reentrant same-owner clear, real scoped late upgrade, adoption after upgrade, and new scoped construction in the destination document.

A separate no-Lit/no-house bare HTMLElement reduction fails in Firefox when a still-undefined scoped element moves to another document before the first definition. Original scoped registry.upgrade(target) and upgrade(shadowRoot) do not repair it. Loading the polyfill in both documents does not repair it. Chromium/WebKit native scoped registries pass this reduction.

The polyfill source registers native stand-in classes through a captured native registry and delegates upgrade through that same registry. That source mechanism is consistent with the observed document-bound failure; no helper handshake/controller exists on the failing raw HTMLElement.

limits: This is a bounded helper/controller fixture with three style properties, not the final77-property renderer or whole component acceptance.
Fixture serializes scalar values into inline styles solely to observe actual overlap. It is not proposed production CSS output.
Define-after-adoption remains an unresolved Firefox/polyfill integration defect; late-before-adoption success does not certify that combination.
No automatic registry workaround was added to the helper, no global monkeypatch added, no source changed by this task.
Compiled fixture source is transpiled with the same TypeScript/Lit transform settings used by scripts/build.ts; this task does not claim a new complete strict typecheck or declaration build.
